description: Five original, non-activated teaching-depth exemplars spanning Grades 1–9. NOT comprehensive curriculum coverage; do not count as mapped, approved or mastered.

packages.title: Place-value regrouping and comparison
packages.existing_family_evidence: Existing elementary number/place-value content; deepen visual-to-symbolic bridge
packages.objective: Explain a three-digit number as hundreds, tens and ones, including exchanges without changing value.
diagnostic: Show 14 ones; ask for equivalent tens-and-ones representation.
Ask learner to explain whether exchanging ten ones changes total.
lesson_sequence: Launch with a familiar concrete situation; elicit an estimate or prediction.
Represent the structure with a manipulable or visual model and ask learners to describe invariants.
Connect each part of the model to a precise equation or representation.
Compare a valid strategy with a plausible misconception and ask for a counterexample.
Fade scaffolds; require a written explanation and a new-context transfer.

worked_examples.question: Build 243 with base-ten blocks.
worked_steps: Place two hundred-flats, four ten-rods, three unit-cubes.

worked_examples.question: Exchange one hundred in 352.
worked_steps: Trade 1 hundred for 10 tens: 2 hundreds, 15 tens, 2 ones.

misconception_pathways.probe: In 582, does the 8 mean eight or eighty?
socratic_hints: Which place contains the 8?
How many ones would eight tens make?
misconception_pathways.remediation: Build eight rods and count 80 ones.

socratic_hints: Can you exchange a hundred for tens?
Does an exchange change the total?
Compare hundreds first.
Then inspect the tens position.
misconception_pathways.remediation: Model both with blocks and compare tens.

independent_assessment.question: 2 hundreds, 13 tens and 6 ones: write the numeral.
Write 705 as hundreds, tens and ones.
Transfer: a school packs 10 pencils per bundle; 340 pencils require how many bundles?

controls: exchange ten units for a ten-rod
exchange ten rods for a hundred-flat
interactive_spec.a11y: keyboard buttons for exchanges, text inventory readout; no visual-only answer
interactive_spec.independent_assessment: read-only numeric entry; no hint events

mastery_gate.require: correct reasoning on independent items plus an unseen transfer; thresholds require independent pedagogical review

provenance.gap_register: PR #325, DRAFT; independent jurisdictional mapping not asserted

packages.title: Equivalent fractions through area and number-line models
packages.existing_family_evidence: Existing fraction comparison/equivalence families and draft PR #309; avoid duplicating generator identity
packages.objective: Construct and justify equivalent fractions by partitioning the same whole.
diagnostic: Present 1/2 and 2/4 on equal-size bars and ask for an explanation.
lesson_sequence: Launch with a familiar concrete situation; elicit an estimate or prediction.
Represent the structure with a manipulable or visual model and ask learners to describe invariants.
Connect each part of the model to a precise equation or representation.
Compare a valid strategy with a plausible misconception and ask for a counterexample.
Fade scaffolds; require a written explanation and a new-context transfer.

worked_examples.question: Show 1/2 and 2/4 with fraction bars.
worked_steps: Split one same-size whole into 2 equal pieces; shade one.
Split an identical whole into 4 equal pieces; shade two.

worked_examples.question: Find a fraction equivalent to 3/5 with denominator 10.
worked_steps: Split each fifth into two equal parts.

worked_examples.question: Simplify 8/12.
worked_steps: Group numerator and denominator in groups of 4.

worked_examples.question: Locate 3/6 on a number line.
worked_steps: Divide 0 to 1 into six equal intervals.

misconception_pathways.probe: Is half of a small pizza always equal to half of a large pizza?
socratic_hints: What must be held fixed to compare fractions?
Does the whole have the same size?
misconception_pathways.remediation: Overlay equal-sized wholes before judging equality.

misconception_pathways.error: Add same amount to numerator and denominator
socratic_hints: Sketch both on equal bars.
What operation preserves the ratio?
misconception_pathways.remediation: Use partition multiplication rather than adding one to both parts.

socratic_hints: Keep the whole fixed.
Which partition makes smaller pieces?
misconception_pathways.remediation: Drag eighths over quarters and compare unit size.

independent_assessment.question: Transfer: two identical-length ribbons have 3/6 and 4/8 colored. Are colored lengths equal?

controls: snap fraction marker to number line
interactive_spec.a11y: fraction quantities announced; keyboard partition and shade controls; reduced motion
interactive_spec.independent_assessment: no fraction-bar scaffold or corrective comparison events

mastery_gate.require: correct reasoning on independent items plus an unseen transfer; thresholds require independent pedagogical review

provenance.gap_register: PR #325, DRAFT; independent jurisdictional mapping not asserted

packages.title: Rectangular-prism volume with fractional dimensions
packages.existing_family_evidence: MATH.GEO.VOLUME.PRISM existing integer generator; PR #325 identifies fractional-depth gap
packages.objective: Use fractional unit-cube partitions to compute exact volume with cubic units.
diagnostic: Show a 1×1×1 cube subdivided into halves on each axis and ask how many eighth-cubes fit.
Ask which unit measures the amount of space in a box.
lesson_sequence: Launch with a familiar concrete situation; elicit an estimate or prediction.
Represent the structure with a manipulable or visual model and ask learners to describe invariants.
Connect each part of the model to a precise equation or representation.
Compare a valid strategy with a plausible misconception and ask for a counterexample.
Fade scaffolds; require a written explanation and a new-context transfer.

worked_examples.question: Find volume of 1/2 m by 3 m by 2 m prism.
worked_steps: Multiply by height 2 to obtain 3 cubic metres.

worked_examples.question: Find volume of 3/2 cm by 2/3 cm by 4 cm.
Find volume of 1/2 by 1/2 by 1/2 unit cube.
worked_steps: One small block occupies 1 of 8 equal cubes.

worked_examples.question: Find volume of 5/4 m by 2 m by 1/2 m.
A box has volume 3/2 m³, width 1/2 m and height 3 m. Find length.

misconception_pathways.probe: Is the volume of a 2×3×4 box 6 cubic units?
socratic_hints: How many layers are stacked?
What dimension did you omit?

misconception_pathways.probe: Can a 1/2×2×2 prism hold 8 unit cubes?
socratic_hints: Compare with a 1×2×2 prism.
How does halving one edge change volume?
misconception_pathways.remediation: Partition along fractional edge and count half-cubes.

misconception_pathways.probe: Is 3/2 cm³ the same unit as 3/2 cm²?
socratic_hints: What does each unit measure?
Count how many spatial dimensions multiply.
misconception_pathways.remediation: Label length, area and volume models explicitly.

independent_assessment.question: Find volume of 3/4 m × 2/3 m × 6 m.
Find volume of 5/2 cm × 4/5 cm × 3/2 cm.
Transfer: volume 9/4 m³, base 3/2 m². Find height.

interactive_spec.scene: 3D rectangular prism with fractional unit partitions
interactive_spec.a11y: text dimensions and exact rational volume; static orthographic alternatives; reduced motion
interactive_spec.independent_assessment: hide cell counts and guided volume labels

mastery_gate.require: correct reasoning on independent items plus an unseen transfer; thresholds require independent pedagogical review

packages.title: Percent commission, fees, and reference-based percent error
packages.existing_family_evidence: MATH.PCT.* discount/tax/markup families exist; PR #325 identifies commission and measured/reference depth
packages.objective: Select the correct reference base and calculate commissions, fees and percent error accurately.
diagnostic: Ask whether a 10% fee on $40 is $4 or $44, and what each represents.
Ask which denominator to use when comparing measured 9 to reference 10.
lesson_sequence: Launch with a familiar concrete situation; elicit an estimate or prediction.
Represent the structure with a manipulable or visual model and ask learners to describe invariants.
Connect each part of the model to a precise equation or representation.
Compare a valid strategy with a plausible misconception and ask for a counterexample.
Fade scaffolds; require a written explanation and a new-context transfer.

worked_examples.question: A salesperson earns 8% of $250 in commission.
A $60 ticket has a 5% service fee.
Measured length 48 cm; reference 50 cm. Find percent error.
worked_steps: Divide by reference 50 cm, multiply by 100.

worked_examples.question: Measured mass 2.1 kg; reference 2.0 kg. Find percent error.

misconception_pathways.probe: Does 8% commission on $250 mean 8% of the $20 commission?
socratic_hints: What quantity is named as the sale price?
Which base does the contract specify?
misconception_pathways.remediation: Highlight sale amount and commission rate separately.

misconception_pathways.error: Percent error divided by measured value
misconception_pathways.probe: Should 48 vs reference 50 use 48 as denominator?
socratic_hints: Which value is the agreed reference?
What does 'percent of reference' mean?
misconception_pathways.remediation: Display measured and reference bars and compare error to reference.

misconception_pathways.probe: Is 5% of $60 the total ticket price?
socratic_hints: Is the question asking for the fee or total?
Which quantity must be added?
misconception_pathways.remediation: Use receipt with base, fee and total separate.

independent_assessment.question: A $160 purchase has a 3% fee; find total.
Transfer: measured 36 m, reference 40 m; find percent error.

interactive_spec.scene: editable invoice and measurement reference bar
interactive_spec.a11y: screen-reader amounts and bases, keyboard percent input, no reliance on color
interactive_spec.independent_assessment: numeric entry only; no revealed base selection

packages.title: Linear relationships from tables, graphs and contexts
packages.existing_family_evidence: Existing algebra/functions families and draft Grade 9 PR #317; deepen multi-representation modeling
packages.objective: Identify slope, intercept and domain assumptions in a linear contextual model.
diagnostic: Compare two tables and identify whether the rate of change is constant.
Ask which part of a taxi bill is paid even for zero distance.
lesson_sequence: Launch with a familiar concrete situation; elicit an estimate or prediction.
Represent the structure with a manipulable or visual model and ask learners to describe invariants.
Connect each part of the model to a precise equation or representation.
Compare a valid strategy with a plausible misconception and ask for a counterexample.
Fade scaffolds; require a written explanation and a new-context transfer.

worked_examples.question: Table: x=0,1,2 and y=3,7,11.
worked_steps: Each x increase of 1 adds 4 to y.

worked_examples.question: A tank starts at 30 L and drains 5 L/min.
Find intersection of y=2x+1 and y=−x+7.

misconception_pathways.probe: In y=3x+7, is 7 the per-unit change?
socratic_hints: What happens when x increases by one?
What is y when x=0?
misconception_pathways.remediation: Build a two-row table to separate initial value and rate.

misconception_pathways.error: Negative slope interpreted as negative starting quantity
socratic_hints: Evaluate t=0.
Which term controls direction of change?
misconception_pathways.remediation: Animate tank with decreasing volume from positive start.

misconception_pathways.probe: Can the draining tank model be used at t=100 minutes?
socratic_hints: When does the tank reach zero?
What does negative water volume mean?
misconception_pathways.remediation: Graph mathematical line and highlight physically meaningful segment.

guided_practice.question: A $10 setup fee plus $3 per item: cost for 4 items
For y=−2x+9 find y at x=3

independent_assessment.question: A subscription costs $6 plus $4 per month. Write cost after m months.
Find slope of line through (−1,2) and (3,10).
Transfer: a tank holds 48 L and loses 6 L/min. When is it empty?

interactive_spec.scene: linked table graph and equation with contextual domain
interactive_spec.a11y: tabular equivalent of graph, keyboard point controls, descriptive axis labels
interactive_spec.independent_assessment: no linked previews; require independent symbolic and contextual reasoning
